source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Flexential Salt Lake City - Millcreek publishes 1.92 MW of IT capacity across 36,000 square feet of technical space. That works out to roughly 53 watts per square foot, a density consistent with mixed enterprise and colocation use rather than purpose-built AI training. As an assumption, at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 1.92 MW of IT load is roughly 48 racks total, which is a small footprint by any measure of modern GPU cluster deployment.

The certifications tell a clear story about intended workload type. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the facility for audited financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for controlled defense and export-regulated data. HITRUST qualifies it for regulated healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the attestation standard underlying the SOC reports. Together these mark a facility built for compliance-sensitive enterprise workloads, not for raw training scale.

Within Utah, this site ranks seventh out of eight facilities with a published megawatt figure, holding 1.92 MW against a mapped-facility total of 51.69 MW across those eight, which is roughly 3.7 percent of the published state capacity this site has read. Twenty-one facilities are mapped in Utah in total, and most publish no capacity figure, so the true state total is larger than what can be calculated here. For a reader focused on AI scaling, Millcreek's significance is as a compliance-capable colocation node, not as a source of meaningful training compute.
